claim_1.claim: Microarray analysis of peripheral blood RNA samples from the discovery cohort of male healthy volunteers and the validation cohort of female healthy volunteers, across days 0, 1, 3, and 14 after vaccination, using mixed model regression analysis with SNPs located in 1-Mb intervals around each expression reporter sequence and Manhattan plots of genotype-expression -log10 p-values across the genome, showed that 467 SNP-transcript pairs corresponding to 78 unique genes passed equally stringent genotype-effect and day-effect thresholds in both cohorts compared to the candidate set of stringent-threshold SNP-transcript pairs assessed in both cohorts.

sources.quote: A majority of these (467 SNP-transcript pairs, corresponding to 78 unique genes) would pass equally stringent thresholds in both cohorts (genotype effect p<5 × 10−8, day effect p<0.01).

Figure 1. Multiple genes show both a transcriptional response to the vaccine and evidence of genetic regulation of gene expression (cis-acting eQTL) in both cohorts.Manhattan plots of the genotype-expression—log10 p-values across the genome for the discovery (inner circle) and validation (outer circle) cohorts. Each dot represents a SNP-transcript pair. Red dots indicate SNP-transcript pairs for which there is evidence of significant genotype-expression association (genotype p<5 × 10−8) and evidence of a transcriptional response to the vaccine (day effect p<0.05). The 78 genes that showed both properties in the two cohorts are shown in the outer margin.

claim_2.claim: Microarray analysis of peripheral blood RNA samples from healthy volunteers ages 18 to 40 years in discovery (males) and validation (females) cohorts, collected on days 0, 1, 3, and 14 after vaccination, using cis-eQTL analysis, showed that 5155 validated eQTL SNP-transcript pairs were identified across the study timepoints in the combined discovery/validation validation scheme.

sources.quote: Using a cis-effect significance threshold of p<1 × 10−4 in the discovery cohort and p<0.05 in the validation cohort, this analysis identified 5155 validated eQTL SNP-transcript pairs (3011 at baseline and 3417, 2496, and 3043 at days 1, 3, and 14, respectively).

claim_3.claim: Microarray analysis of peripheral blood RNA samples from healthy volunteers ages 18 to 40 years in discovery (males) and validation (females) cohorts, collected on days 0, 1, 3, and 14 after vaccination, using cis-eQTL analysis, showed that the 5155 validated eQTL SNP-transcript pairs corresponded to 543 unique genes.

sources.quote: These SNP-transcript pairs correspond to 543 unique genes.

claim_4.claim: Microarray analysis of peripheral blood RNA samples from healthy volunteers ages 18 to 40 years in discovery (males) and validation (females) cohorts, collected on days 0, 1, 3, and 14 after vaccination, using additive genotype-effect modeling and delta-Rg2 analysis, showed that multiple loci had genetic effects on expression that were enhanced or only apparent after vaccination compared to baseline.

sources.quote: We then identified the SNP-transcript pairs in which the expression variance explained was most strongly increased after vaccination (highest change in genetic variance explained, which we termed delta-Rg2). This analysis revealed multiple loci at which the genetic effect was either enhanced or only apparent after the experimental perturbation.

claim_5.claim: Microarray analysis of peripheral blood RNA samples from healthy volunteers ages 18 to 40 years in discovery (males) and validation (females) cohorts, collected on days 0 and 3 after vaccination, using cis-eQTL analysis of SNP-transcript pairs that show a strong cis-eQTL and a transcriptional response to vaccination, showed that the strength of the genotype effect on expression (slope of the additive association; β) increased after vaccination compared to baseline and was the main driver of the observed increase in the genetic effect (R2g), while within-genotype variance (MSE) was unchanged.

sources.quote: Figure 2B shows that an increase in the strength of the genotype effect (slope of the additive association) was the main driver for the observed change in Rg2

(B) An increase in R2g after the experimental perturbation is a general feature of the SNP-transcript pairs that show a strong cis-eQTLs and a transcriptional response to vaccination (left). The within-genotype variance is unchanged (MSE, center), while the strength of the genotype effect on expression (slope of the additive association; β, right) increases, suggesting that the latter is the main driver for the observed increase in the genetic effect after vaccination.

claim_6.claim: Microarray analysis of peripheral blood RNA samples from healthy volunteers ages 18 to 40 years in discovery (males) and validation (females) cohorts, collected on days 0 and 3 after vaccination, using cis-eQTL analysis of SNP-transcript pairs that show a strong cis-eQTL and a transcriptional response to vaccination, showed that an increase in the genetic effect (R2g) after vaccination was a general feature of the SNP-transcript pairs that show a strong cis-eQTL and a transcriptional response to vaccination compared to baseline.

sources.quote: and that this amplitude change was a general feature of the loci in which we observed both a strong cis-acting eQTL and a transcriptional response to the vaccine stimulus.

(B) An increase in R2g after the experimental perturbation is a general feature of the SNP-transcript pairs that show a strong cis-eQTLs and a transcriptional response to vaccination (left). The within-genotype variance is unchanged (MSE, center), while the strength of the genotype effect on expression (slope of the additive association; β, right) increases, suggesting that the latter is the main driver for the observed increase in the genetic effect after vaccination.

claim_7.claim: Microarray analysis of peripheral blood RNA samples from healthy volunteers ages 18 to 40 years in discovery (males) and validation (females) cohorts, collected on days 0, 1, 3, and 14 after vaccination, using Spearman's rank correlation analysis of delta-Rg2 values across all SNP-transcript pairs, showed that delta-Rg2 values in the discovery cohort were positively associated with delta-Rg2 values in the validation cohort.

sources.quote: The delta-Rg2 values were consistent between the cohorts when evaluated by Spearman’s rank correlation analysis using all SNP-transcript pairs (Cor = 0.25, p<2 × 10−16).

claim_8.claim: Microarray analysis of peripheral blood RNA samples from healthy volunteers ages 18 to 40 years in discovery (males) and validation (females) cohorts, collected on days 0, 1, 3, and 14 after vaccination, using delta-Rg2 ranking and cis-eQTL significance filtering, showed that 146 SNP-transcript pairs were in the top 1% of the delta-Rg2 distribution and also showed evidence of a strong cis-acting eQTL in both cohorts.

sources.quote: To select a conservative set of candidate loci based on this property for further analysis, we identified the SNP-transcript pairs that were in the top 1% of the delta-Rg2 distribution and also showed evidence of a strong cis-acting eQTL (genotype effect p<5 × 10−8), in both cohorts. Data for the resulting set of 146 SNP-transcript pairs, including Rg2 values, are provided in Table 2

claim_9.claim: DNA microarray analysis of whole blood from healthy volunteers ages 18 to 40 years in the discovery and validation cohorts after influenza vaccination on day 0, using content analysis on the list of 98 genes with a strong cis-eQTL and a response to vaccination expressed as either a transcriptional response or a change in the genetic effect in both cohorts, showed significant enrichment for genes involved in membrane trafficking, antigen processing, and antigen presentation.

sources.quote: Content analysis on the union of the two sets (98 genes) showed significant enrichment for genes involved in antigen processing and presentation, cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-mediated apoptosis of target cells, dendritic cell maturation and function, and membrane trafficking (Figure 3).

Figure 3. Content analysis shows enrichment for genes involved in membrane trafficking, antigen processing, and antigen presentation.Barplots show categories with significant overrepresentation in the list of 98 genes with a strong cis-eQTL and a response to vaccination expressed as either a transcriptional response or a change in the genetic effect in both cohorts. The negative log(p-value) is plotted on the x-axis.

claim_10.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from the combined discovery and validation cohorts after influenza vaccination on day 0, using linear modeling of expression values across the time course, showed that 301 genes had significant correlation between gene expression and the antibody response to the vaccine in both cohorts.

sources.quote: In a combined analysis of the two cohorts in the present study, 301 transcripts were found to correlate with the magnitude of the antibody response (Figure 4).
(B) A total of 301 genes showed evidence of significant correlation between gene expression and the antibody response to the vaccine in both cohorts.

claim_11.claim: Microarray analysis of whole blood from the two independent cohorts after influenza vaccination on day 0, using integrative genomic analysis, showed that the 20 genes TAP2, SNX29, FGD2, NAPSA, NAPSB, GM2A, C1orf85, JUP, FBLN5, CHST13, DIP2A, PAM, D4S234E, C3AR1, HERC2, LST1, LRRC37A4, OAS1, RPL14, and DYNLT1 met combined criteria of significant genotype-expression association, significant correlation between transcriptional and antibody responses, and either a transcriptional response to the vaccine or a change in the magnitude of the genetic effect after vaccination.

sources.quote: We imposed an additional selection threshold based on this correlation, and identified 20 genes that show evidence of significant genotype-expression association (genotype effect p<5 × 10−8), a significant correlation between the transcriptional and antibody responses (expression-antibody effect p<0.05), and either a transcriptional response to the vaccine (day effect p<0.01) or evidence of a change in the magnitude of the genetic effect after vaccination (top 1% of the delta-Rg2 distribution) in the two independent cohorts.

These loci have the strongest evidence of genetic variation influencing the immune response to the vaccine, and include TAP2, SNX29, FGD2, NAPSA, NAPSB, GM2A, C1orf85, JUP, FBLN5, CHST13, DIP2A, PAM, D4S234E, C3AR1, HERC2, LST1, LRRC37A4, OAS1, RPL14, and DYNLT1.

claim_12.claim: DNA microarray analysis of whole blood from the combined discovery and validation cohorts across days 0, 1, 3, and 14 after vaccination, using linear modeling of expression against titer response index, showed that 301 transcripts were associated with the magnitude of the antibody response to the vaccine.

sources.quote: In a combined analysis of the two cohorts in the present study, 301 transcripts were found to correlate with the magnitude of the antibody response (Figure 4).

claim_13.claim: DNA microarray analysis of whole blood from the two independent cohorts across days 0, 1, 3, and 14 after vaccination, using thresholding on genotype effect, expression-antibody correlation, and transcriptional response to vaccination, showed that 20 genes had significant genotype-expression association, significant correlation between the transcriptional and antibody responses, and a transcriptional response to vaccination.

sources.quote: We imposed an additional selection threshold based on this correlation, and identified 20 genes that show evidence of significant genotype-expression association (genotype effect p<5 × 10−8), a significant correlation between the transcriptional and antibody responses (expression-antibody effect p<0.05), and either a transcriptional response to the vaccine (day effect p<0.01) or evidence of a change in the magnitude of the genetic effect after vaccination (top 1% of the delta-Rg2 distribution) in the two independent cohorts.

Figure 5. Genetic variation in intracellular antigen transport and processing influences the human immune response to influenza vaccination.20 genes show evidence of a transcriptional response to vaccination, significant genotype effects on gene expression, and correlation between the transcriptional and antibody responses.

claim_14.claim: DNA microarray analysis of whole blood from the two independent cohorts across days 0, 1, 3, and 14 after vaccination, using thresholding on genotype effect, expression-antibody correlation, and transcriptional response to vaccination, showed that the 20 genes meeting these criteria included TAP2, SNX29, FGD2, NAPSA, NAPSB, GM2A, C1orf85, JUP, FBLN5, CHST13, DIP2A, PAM, D4S234E, C3AR1, HERC2, LST1, LRRC37A4, OAS1, RPL14, and DYNLT1.

claim_15.claim: Illumina HumanOmniExpress microarray analysis of peripheral blood genomic DNA from healthy volunteers ages 18 to 40 years in the discovery and validation cohorts after vaccination on day 0, using association tests and an empirical quantile-quantile plot of 137 SNP-transcript pairs with evidence of a strong cis-eQTL, a dynamic response to the vaccine, and correlation between the transcriptional and antibody responses against the entire data set background SNPs, showed that the empirical quantile-quantile plot for the 137 result SNPs significantly deviated from the empirical distribution of the entire data set background SNPs.

sources.quote: We determined genetic associations to the antibody response using 137 eQTL SNPs from these 20 loci. The quantile-quantile plot from the association tests performed on these SNPs shows marked deviation from the empirical null distribution for QTL associations (Figure 6), supporting the idea that these loci are enriched for true genetic associations.

Figure 6. SNPs at the 20 loci identified show evidence of association with the antibody response to the vaccine.137 SNP-transcript pairs with evidence of a strong cis-eQTL, a dynamic response to the vaccine (a change in transcript abundance or in the magnitude of the genetic effect), and correlation between the transcriptional and antibody responses were selected (result SNPs, in red). The empirical quantile-quantile plot of the result SNPs shows significant deviation from the empirical distribution of the entire data set (background SNPs, in blue).

claim_16.claim: Microarray analysis of peripheral blood RNA samples from healthy volunteers ages 18 to 40 years in the discovery and validation cohorts, obtained on days 0, 1, 3, and 14 after vaccination on day 0, using extended causal modeling with independent-versus-reactive and independent-versus-causal hypothesis tests, showed that patterns in the 137 eQTL SNP-transcript pairs from the 20 loci with the strongest evidence of genetic variation influencing the immune response to the vaccine trended toward the causal model compared to the reactive model.

sources.quote: We found that the patterns in the data trend toward the causal model compared to the reactive model (Figure 7B), but a power analysis based on the distribution of the empirical effect sizes of our observed associations also indicates that our sample size is too modest to support definitive conclusions (Figure 7C).

(B) p-values for independent-versus-reactive and independent-versus-causal hypothesis tests. Each point shows the result for one SNP-transcript pair. Points to the right of the solid vertical line are significant (p<0.05) for the reactive hypothesis and points above the solid horizontal line are significant for the causal hypothesis. The dashed line shows a p=0.1 threshold.

claim_17.claim: Microarray analysis of peripheral blood RNA samples from healthy volunteers ages 18 to 40 years in the discovery and validation cohorts, obtained on days 0, 1, 3, and 14 after vaccination on day 0, using power analysis of rejection of the independent hypothesis on simulated non-independent data with effect sizes and variances similar to those in the enrichment set, showed that the combined sample size in the study was too modest to support definitive conclusions.

sources.quote: We found that the patterns in the data trend toward the causal model compared to the reactive model (Figure 7B), but a power analysis based on the distribution of the empirical effect sizes of our observed associations also indicates that our sample size is too modest to support definitive conclusions (Figure 7C).

(C) Power for rejection of the independent hypothesis. Non-independent data were simulated with effect sizes and variances similar to those in the enrichment set (the set of SNP-transcript pairs that were found to be significant in our study). The curve shows the proportion of cases in which the simulated data rejected the independent (null) hypothesis. The dotted line indicates the combined sample size in our study.
